name: The Harrowgate Museum of Tides and Tools
hours: Closed on Mondays and on 25 December
tickets: Adult: 14 pounds. Concession (65+, students): 9 pounds. Under 12s: free.
Family pass (2 adults + up to 3 children): 36 pounds.
Thursday after 17:30 is pay-what-you-like, no booking needed.
Tickets can be changed to another day up to 24 hours ahead at no cost.
exhibits: Ground floor: 'The Salt Engine', a working 1890s tidal pump, steam-demonstrated at 11:00 and 14:00.
First floor: 'Lanterns of the Estuary', 40 lighthouse lenses and ship's lamps (until 28 February).
Second floor: 'Hands On', a workshop gallery where visitors try rope work and brass rubbing; sessions on the hour, ages 6+.
Basement: 'Drowned Streets', a walk-through model of the old harbour town.
accessibility: Step-free entrance on Wharf Lane; lifts reach every floor except the Drowned Streets basement, which has a steep ramp.
Wheelchairs and folding stools can be borrowed free at the front desk.
Quiet hour every Tuesday 10:00 to 11:00: lights dimmed, sounds off, the steam demonstration is skipped.
Assistance dogs are welcome. Large-print guides and a tactile floor plan are available at the desk.
escalation: For anything not covered here, offer the front desk line (01632 960 418) rather than guessing.
